Monaire is building the infrastructure layer for intelligent commercial HVAC. We combine on-device sensors, smart thermostats, and machine-learning systems to automate control, surface real operational insight, and materially reduce energy waste at scale. This is not offline modeling or notebook ML. Models run in production, interact with physical systems, and must be observable, debuggable, and correct. The platform spans edge devices, cloud services, streaming pipelines, control logic, and ML inference.

Engineers here work on:

• Data ingestion and streaming at scale from heterogeneous hardware

• Low-latency decision pipelines and control loops

• ML systems that survive missing data, drift, and adversarial real-world conditions

• Infrastructure for model deployment, monitoring, and rollback

• Apps and services that customers depend on to run their buildings every day

You will work closely with backend engineers, product managers, and domain experts to translate raw sensor data into reliable models that power customer-facing features and internal decision-making.

Bachelor's/Master's/PhD in CS, IT, Applied Math, Statistics, or related field

COMMERCIAL MANAGER WEST

Location: US West (remote), strong interest for San Francisco

THE ROLE

Our commercial segment is one of the more technically demanding sales environments in the industry. Our buyers are data engineers, platform architects, and technical founders - and the AEs who succeed here do so because they can meet those buyers as peers, not vendors. Building and leading that team requires someone who has done it themselves and knows what great looks like.

As Manager of Commercial Sales at ClickHouse, you'll own the performance, development, and culture of our Commercial AE team. You'll be expected to live in the details - reviewing pipelines, sitting on calls, pressure-testing deal strategy, and knowing every meaningful opportunity in the book. The best managers in this role won't be directing from a distance; they'll be the person their reps turn to when a deal gets complicated. This is not a role for someone who wants to manage from a dashboard. It's a role for someone who wants to build something.

You'll inherit a team that has real momentum, as our Commercial segment represents a significant % of our overall business.

WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING

- Lead, coach, and develop a team of Commercial Account Executives selling into the sub-250 employee segment - helping them close faster, think more technically, and operate with greater autonomy over time.

- Own the Commercial segment number. You're accountable for team attainment, pipeline health, and forecast accuracy - and you'll be expected to have a clear point of view on both at any given moment.

- Spend time in deals. Review deals, join customer conversations when it matters, and help your reps navigate the technical and commercial complexity that defines this segment.

- Hire exceptional people. The Commercial AE profile is rare: technically credible, commercially hungry, and able to operate without hand-holding. You know how to find and close that person.

- Build the playbook. Document what's working, codify best practices, and create repeatable frameworks for technical discovery, objection handling, and deal progression that the team can scale.

- Partner cross-functionally with Solutions Engineering, Product, and Marketing to ensure the Commercial team has the support, enablement, and feedback loops they need to win.

- Identify patterns across the pipeline - where deals stall, where we lose, and where we consistently win - and use those insights to improve team performance and inform product and GTM decisions.

- Contribute to the broader Commercial strategy, including segmentation, coverage model, and how we evolve the motion as the team scales.

WHAT YOU BRING

- A track record of success as a quota-carrying AE in a technical sales environment - you've sold data infrastructure, developer tooling, or a similarly technical product to engineering buyers and you know what that motion actually requires.

- Experience leading or mentoring other sellers, whether in a formal management role or as a senior IC who took ownership of team development. You know how to coach, not just direct.

- Technical credibility. You don't need to be an engineer, but you need to earn respect in rooms full of them. You understand the modern data stack, can hold a conversation about architecture, and know enough to identify when a deal is stalling for technical reasons vs. commercial ones.

- Strong commercial instincts. You can read a pipeline, spot sandbagging, identify risk early, and have an honest forecast conversation with leadership without needing a week to prepare.

- A builder mentality. The playbook is still being written. You're comfortable operating in that environment and energized by the opportunity to shape it rather than frustrated by the ambiguity.

- Genuine investment in people development. Your reps' growth is your growth. You give direct feedback, create space for people to fail safely, and take accountability for the development of everyone on your team.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Data Infrastructure
description:
About Backblaze

Backblaze is the object storage leader in the open cloud movement, fueling customer success with cloud storage built purposefully to unlock budgets, unburden administrators, and unleash innovators. Together with our partners, we’re helping customers break free from the restrictive, overpriced legacy solutions that hold them back, and blaze forward with the full power of the open cloud in their hands.

Founded in 2007, we scaled the business with less than $3 million in outside funding until 2021, when we did a traditional IPO on the Nasdaq stock exchange. Today, Backblaze generates over $100m in revenue and is the leading specialized storage cloud - managing over three billion gigabytes of data storage for 500K+ customers in 175+ countries, including businesses, developers, IT professionals, and individuals.

Want to know what you’ll be doing?

You will work on our data infrastructure platform which supports the B2 Object Storage and Computer Backup products, responsible for the data infrastructure that everything runs on. You will help improve automation, observability and stability for durability, increase throughput, and drive architectural changes to support the long term requirements of our service. 

Responsibilities:

• Design and build automation frameworks that let other engineers provision, configure, and repair fleet infrastructure themselves

• Design and extend the observability stack (metrics, logs, traces, alerts) that tells us whether the storage platform is healthy and where it is degrading

• Build reporting, dashboards, and visualizations that give engineering and leadership a clear view into fleet health, capacity, and operational trends

• Build system health tooling that detects failing hardware, drifting configuration, and capacity risk before they turn into incidents

• Lead technical design discussions and produce clear design documents for changes that span multiple services and teams

• Drive the implementation of large features from design through rollout, including the migration and backfill work that real systems require

• Partner with the on-call rotation to turn recurring toil and incident findings into automation and better signal

The Right Fit:

• 7+ years of backend development in an enterprise environment, working in an object-oriented or systems language (Java, Rust, C++, C#, Go, or similar)

• Experience designing automation frameworks or platforms that other engineers build on

• Experience building large scale software systems running on thousands of servers

• Experience building automation or tooling that other engineers depend on daily, whether internal platform services, operational tooling, or a deployment and configuration pipeline

• Working knowledge of an observability stack (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, ELK, Datadog, or equivalent), including instrumenting a service and designing alerts people trust

• Strong Linux fundamentals and comfort operating in a bare-metal or hybrid environment rather than a fully managed cloud

• Professional experience incorporating AI-assisted development tools (Gemini, Cursor, Claude Code, or similar)

• Comfortable with all aspects of the software development lifecycle, including design, implementation, testing, and rollout

• Exhibits curiosity and seeks to understand before offering solutions

• Communicates proactively in a remote environment by keeping the team informed, surfacing blockers early, and moving work forward

• Applies analytical thinking to ambiguous problems

Bonus points for:

• Proficiency in Java

• Experience with configuration management or infrastructure-as-code tooling (Ansible, Salt, Puppet, Chef, Terraform)

• Experience designing SLOs and error budgets, or reducing alert noise on a fleet running at scale

• Experience with time-series databases and query languages such as PromQL

• Experience automating hardware lifecycle work: burn-in, failure detection, drive replacement, decommissioning

title: Data Center Power Generation and Microgrids Engineer
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle. The loads involved are large enough - and arrive fast enough - that utility supply alone often can't meet the need on the timeline required, and the step-load behavior of large accelerator clusters creates power-quality and ride-through demands that conventional backup-generation designs weren't built for. Anthropic's Data Center Infrastructure team is responsible for solving that problem: delivering facilities that can be energized early, ride through grid disturbances, and present a well-behaved load at the point of interconnection (POI).

 

As a Data Center Power Generation & Microgrids Engineer, you'll own the behind-the-meter generation and storage architecture for Anthropic's data center portfolio. That means the on-site generation fleet - reciprocating engine gensets, gas turbines, fuel cells - and the battery energy storage systems that buffer load steps and provide ride-through. It means the microgrid layer that ties them together: islanding and resynchronization, black-start, load-shedding, and generation dispatch. And it means the grid side: interconnection studies and agreements, IEEE 1547/2800 compliance, and power quality at the point of interconnection. You'll also own our temporary- and bridging-generation strategies - the plans that let a site energize and start serving load before permanent utility service is available, and transition cleanly once it is.

This is a deeply cross-functional role. You'll work closely with colleagues across the infrastructure team on where and how generation and storage tie into the site electrical distribution, controls, and SCADA, and with our hardware and compute teams to understand the load characteristics you're designing against. You'll be Anthropic's technical counterpart to on-site generation providers, BESS integrators, utilities, and ISOs/RTOs. Expect roughly 20-35% travel for design reviews, factory witness testing, and site startup.

Responsibilities

On-site generation engineering

•
Own Anthropic's behind-the-meter generation architecture across the portfolio - prime-mover selection and sizing (reciprocating engines, gas turbines, fuel cells), paralleling topology, redundancy, fuel systems, and emissions controls - and maintain the generation basis of design and technical specifications that build partners and generation providers design against

•
Set the day-one vs. day-N plant sizing and expansion strategy - what the plant needs on day one so it can be expanded or augmented later, and how to add units, storage, or a grid tie to a system already running

•
Characterize the data center load for external generation partners - step changes, ramps, oscillation, fault behavior, and non-IT load - so providers can size and tune their plant against the real duty

•
Model generation response against the load profile of large-scale ML training - step-load acceptance, block loading, transient frequency and voltage response, load rejection - and set the acceptance criteria (e.g., per ISO 8528-5) that generation packages are tested against

•
Develop temporary- and bridging-generation strategies that deliver early site energization ahead of permanent utility service, including the sequencing, protection, and controls changes needed to transition from temporary to permanent power without stranding equipment or capacity
